There’s been all sorts flying round in the ether about just what kind of show this latest edition to the Trek Universe will be. Videos by ComicBook.com Luckily, Trek legend Jonathan Frakes may have just given longtime fans exactly the kind of update they’ve been hoping for. In conversation with TrekMovie.com on the All Access Star Trek podcast , the Next Generation icon opened up about his work on Star Trek: Starfleet Academy —and his comments about its tone, cast, and storytelling are certainly raising expectations for what promises to be an ambitious new era for Starfleet: “To its credit, Academy has lots of levity. First of all, Paul Giamatti is the villain. And I met him while he was there, and I am a massive fan of his—I think most actors are, and most people are. And I said, ‘How’s it been?’ He said, ‘I have been having such a good time.’ And then he leans in and says, ‘Maybe too good a time.’” Starfleet Academy Brings Back a Classic Trek Ingredient Paul Giamatti in Star Trek: Starfleet Academy Photo Credit: Miller Mobley/Paramount+ Frakes, who directed the penultimate episode of the show’s upcoming first season, revealed to TrekMovie.com that Starfleet Academy may have a youthful cast and fresh setting, but it isn’t abandoning the humor that makes classic Trek shows so enduring. Although Giamatti’s villain doesn’t appear in the episode Frakes directed, he reportedly saw enough of Giamatti’s performance to know that viewers are in for something special. While Strange New Worlds , especially in its third and most recent series, has thrived on switching things up and experimenting with multiple genres and has erred (perhaps too far) into comedy on occasions, Frakes revealed on the podcast that Academy will have a more consistent tone while still containing plenty of funny moments. “I search out the levity in any script, especially in the Treks… because there’s so much… And [on Academy ] it’s there,” Frakes explained to TrekMovie.com “And it helps the rhythm of the cutting and the storytelling.” Read Next Star Trek’s Future Now Has the Same Problem As Its Oldest Sci-Fi Rival It’s perhaps unsurprising that comedy will still be a big feature of the series, with a writer’s room that includes comedic talent such as Lower Decks star and comedian Tawny Newsome. With a cast full of returning Trek comic relief favorites such as Tig Notaro reprising her role as Jett Reno from Star Trek: Discovery (now a member of the faculty at the Academy), Stephen Colbert ( The Late Show ) as the voice of the “Digital Dean of Students” and Robert Picardo (adding his trademark humour returning as the EMH Doctor from Voyager ), the series appears to be aiming for something fun, character-centric, and accessible — without losing the emotional stakes or sci-fi depth that fans expect. For longtime fans who have been missing the more consistent blend of drama, charm, and character-driven humour that defined shows like The Next Generation , Deep Space Nine , and Voyager , Frakes’ comments bode well. Why Old-School Fans Should Be Encouraged Holly Hunter on Star Fleet Academy Frakes has been part of Trek, on-screen and behind the camera, for more than 35 years, so it’s safe to say he knows what he’s talking about, and after such glowing reports, fans will be looking forward to a promising new series that hopefully won’t lose sight of the tone that has anchored Trek for decades. Frakes also singled out Oscar winner Holly Hunter—who plays Captain Nahla Ake, the new 422-year-old, half-Lanthonite chancellor of Starfleet Academy—as a standout presence on set. Describing her as “well-prepared, instinctive, smart, clever,” Frakes praised her command of the role with the kind of enthusiasm that should grab the attention of even the most sceptical of fans. For years, certain corners of the fandom have argued that modern Trek series have occasionally drifted too far into darker, heavier storytelling or too far towards the comedic side. While Star Trek has always explored serious themes and given us plenty of laughs, it’s that unique balance of earnestness, warmth, wit, and morality that has helped the franchise endure. Frakes’ comments suggest that Starfleet Academy has nailed that balance. Most encouraging of all is that this isn’t just lip service. When Frakes, of all people, says the tone feels right, old-school fans have every reason to trust him. And if he’s right, this series might just deliver the nuanced tone fans have been asking for. He later wrote, “Sally Kirkland devours ‘Anna’ like a raw steak and emerges a major star.” Beyond the big screen, Kirkland made her mark on television too. She appeared in popular shows like ‘Roseanne’, ‘Felicity’, ‘Days of Our Lives’, and ‘Valley of the Dolls’ often portraying bold layered women with a spark of rebellion that mirrored her real-life personality. The latest report details when audiences may learn more as the film progresses through development. Interest continues to build as the project moves forward at Amazon MGM Studios . Compulsive Liar starring Kumail Nanjiani and Emily V. Gordon finds studio Amazon MGM Studios has acquired Compulsive Liar, a comedy project from Emily V. Gordon and Kumail Nanjiani, according to Deadline . The studio confirmed that Nanjiani is attached to star and that 21 Laps and Gaumont will produce. The package follows the pair’s previous work on The Big Sick, which earned an Academy Award nomination for Best Original Screenplay. Gordon and Nanjiani will serve as executive producers alongside Holly Brown for Gaumont and Émile Gaudreault. Compulsive Liar adapts the Quebec comedy Menteur, written by Émile Gaudreault, Éric K. Boulianne, and Sébastien Ravary and directed by Gaudreault. The original film follows Simon, a habitual liar whose family and coworkers stage an intervention. When he rejects them, he wakes up to find that every lie he has told has become real. Emily Feher is overseeing the adaptation for 21 Laps. Shawn Levy and Dan Levine produce for 21 Laps, and Nicolas Atlan and Sidonie Dumas produce for Gaumont. In 2024, Gordon launched the production company Winter Coat with Nanjiani and signed a first look deal with Sony Television. Nanjiani and Gordon earned an Academy Award nomination for The Big Sick, which starred Kumail Nanjiani, Holly Hunter, Zoe Kazan, and Ray Romano. The film won Best First Screenplay at the Film Independent Spirit Awards and Best Comedy at the Critics Choice Awards and received multiple major guild and industry nominations. It also appeared on the American Film Institute Top 10 Movies of the Year list. Nanjiani recently announced his new stand up special Night Thoughts, set to debut on Hulu on December 19. His television credits include Only Murders in the Building, Poker Face, Welcome to Chippendales, Obi Wan, Little America, Silicon Valley, Very Young Frankenstein, and Fallout season two. His upcoming films include Ella McCay, Driver’s Ed, and The Breadwinner. It’s got it all — a turkey, an eccentric aunt, a gay brother, men playing football in the yard, in-laws who can’t stand each other, and multiple family meltdowns. Just like yours! Directed by Jodie Foster and released 30 years ago, on November 3, 1995, the film has aged into a cult classic. Now, it’s back for the holidays — streaming on Paramount+ . Home for the Holidays stars Holly Hunter as Claudia Larson, a single mom and art restorer who’s just been laid off and reluctantly heads home to Baltimore for Thanksgiving . There, she reunites with her loving but chaotic parents ( Anne Bancroft and Charles Durning ), her exuberant brother Tommy ( Robert Downey Jr . ), and her judgmental sister Joanne ( Cynthia Stevenson ). The extended family gathering includes Dylan McDermott, Geraldine Chaplin, Claire Danes , Steve Guttenberg, and David Strathairn. What Is 'Home for the Holidays' Really About? On the surface, it’s a comedy about turkey dinners gone wrong, but as Foster put it in a recent interview, the movie was “about that very particular time in your life when you’re 30 and you’re still kind of attached to your parents … You feel infantilized by them, and you’re asking, ‘Did I choose this life? Is this the life I want?’” Foster also recalled that Robert Downey Jr. , then in the throes of addiction, brought an unpredictable energy to the set. “He was 100% present, as far as I was concerned,” she said. “His pain is onscreen. In some ways, it was good for the movie.” Downey Jr.’s improvisations, like the infamous “car monologue” scene, gave Tommy a manic charm that still makes the performance unforgettable. While it only modestly recouped its budget in 1995, Home for the Holidays has become a yearly favorite for those who crave a more honest, funny, and chaotic look at family life. It’s unsentimental, but it's still pretty affectionate. It's a Thanksgiving movie that knows gratitude often comes wrapped in awkwardness and regret. “I think we always knew it was a perennial,” Foster reflected. “We hoped people would buy it on DVD, and watch it over and over as time went on. So, as far as I’m concerned, that’s great. ” Home for the Holidays is now streaming on Paramount+ — just in time for the annual parade, the turkey, and the inevitable meltdown. By George Lewis Published: 03 November 2025 We may be accustomed to comebacks in the Marvel Cinematic Universe , with several big names returning to old roles. It\'s no different for some of the stars from the X-Men franchise — but not all of them. Famke Janssen, who portrayed Jean Grey/Phoenix in four films across the series over a 14-year period, has confirmed she hasn\'t been asked to reprise her role since Marvel acquired the rights to the characters. "Never. Never ever," she told Entertainment Weekly . "Every time I do an interview, it\'s mentioned. It\'s interesting. I didn\'t realise that was such a big part. Every interview I do, that will come up. "I should be flattered, I suppose, that this character has resonated with people. It\'s been so long, but it\'s nice that people are still talking about her. I\'m sure every single time there\'s a new [film] that they\'re doing, like Avengers: Doomsday , it\'ll come up again." What to Read Next While it doesn\'t appear that Janssen will be in the fifth film in the Avengers series , there are several X-Men stars returning. Kelsey Grammer, Patrick Stewart, Ian McKellen, Alan Cumming, James Marsden and Rebecca Romijn are all reprising their respective roles. Despite the positive critical reception and whopping commercial success, it\'s currently unclear if Wolverine will be part of Avengers: Doomsday . Jackman certainly wasn\'t letting anything slip when speaking on The View in June. Aside from the slew of X-Men stars, the cast for Avengers: Doomsday is stacked, with Florence Pugh, Sebastian Stan, Robert Downey Jr, Chris Hemsworth, Vanessa Kirby, Pedro Pascal, Joseph Quinn and Anthony Mackie all set to appear. While many of her former co-stars are returning for the upcoming Marvel movie, Janssen previously revealed that Marvel Studios has not contacted her about reprising her role. Famke Janssen elaborates on not being in Avengers: Doomsday Famke Janssen recently sat down for a chat with Kristian Harloff in which she revealed why she would not join the cast of Avengers: Doomsday as her X-Men character. I tend to look forward. That’s not what they want from me.” Furthermore, she conveyed that she is inclined towards having a more creative role when working on a project. However, Janssen said that she is “not opposed to doing anything that’s just being part of a fun ensemble.” While talking to Entertainment Weekly in October 2025, Janssen shared that questions about Avengers: Doomsday are frequent whenever she has interviews. She said, “Every time I do an interview, it’s mentioned. The next two Avengers movies will set up Doctor Doom as the next big bad as heroes from different Earths arrive in the Marvel Cinematic Universe, and fans can finally see the Fox heroes from the X-Men and Fantastic Four meeting up with the MCU Avengers for what should be a fun crossover battle. Names like Patrick Stewart, Ian McKellen, James Marsden, Kelsey Grammer, Alan Cumming, and Rebecca Romijn are all confirmed to appear. However, one other original X-Men actor said they won’t be back. Videos by ComicBook.com In a recent interview with Kristian Harloff , Famke Janssen discussed her past movies and what was coming next for her career, including her new Netflix series, Amsterdam Empire . In the interview, Harloff asked if Janssen had been asked to return for Avengers: Doomsday , and she admitted that she is not returning and wasn’t interested in the opportunity. She said that she is an executive producer on Amsterdam Empire and has a seat at the table where she has a say in things that need to be changed. “I would not be asked back on Doomsday , or somewhere else, with that type of input. That’s not what they want from me,” she admitted. Janssen also said that she prefers not to look back and wants to keep moving forward in her career. “It’s hard for me now to just look back and worry, or think about a part where I get a few lines,” she said. “It just doesn’t seem that interesting to me. I’m in a different place, and I’ve earned my way into this moment, and I’m running with it, because this is 80 films under my belt, and I’ve paid my dues . “ However, Famke Janssen admitted that she isn’t opposed to doing something like Avengers: Doomsday , where she would be part of a fun ensemble. “But at this moment in time, I just finished a movie yesterday in Bulgaria, called One Second After , and I also designed my clothes on that one as well,” she admitted. “It’s so cool to have these added parts to it, what I’m doing in my life right now, because I love creativity. I’m always looking to create.” Read Next Avengers: Doomsday Shows How Much the MCU’s Power Level Has Changed (& It’s a Problem) Famke Janssen Skipping Avengers: Doomsday Is Best For Both Parties Image Courtesy of Fox Famke Janssen was solid as Jean Grey in X-Men, but honestly, it is better for her to remain away from Avengers: Doomsday for a couple of important reasons. First, as Janssen said, she has become more of a player with a seat at the table on her recent projects. While it might be fun to come back in a nostalgic role, it isn’t the best thing for her right now as she continues to find her place as a veteran actor. However, even more important is the fact that this movie is going to have way too many heroes showing up anyway. Why would someone who is finally gaining respect behind the scenes want to come back for what would likely be a performance with a couple of lines, and then possibly get killed off by the end? Janssen finished her role as Jean Grey by dying in X-Men: The Last Stand , and honestly, it might be better to bring back Sophie Turner as Jean Grey since she showed she survived in her world in Dark Phoenix . The fact that the original X-Men are all that has been advertised is telling, and at their ages, it is almost assured they will not last to the reboot following Avengers: Secret Wars . New X-Men heroes need to emerge to carry on that role, and Famke Janssen’s Jean Grey is part of an era that has already moved on. Also, remember, Jean Grey killed Cyclops in X-Men: The Last Stand . Since James Marsden is returning, it proves that this isn’t the world that Jean died on, so it is likely better not to bring Janssen back, considering the confusion it could cause mainstream fans when the X-Men step into the MCU for the first time. By Stefania Sarrubba Published: 30 October 2025 Netflix Netflix might\'ve just dropped your next binge watch with Dutch crime drama Amsterdam Empire , starring Famke Janssen as a woman hellbent on revenge. Announced last year as a "captivating" crime series set in the coffee shops of the Dutch capital, Amsterdam Empire is now available to stream on Netflix. Created by Nico Moolenaar, Bart Uytdenhouwen and Piet Matthys, the seven-part crime drama stars Jacob Derwig as Jack van Doorn, the founder of coffeeshop empire The Jackal. What to Read Next Jack has become rich and famous by fighting off criminals, competitors and Dutch laws, but his empire is threatened when his affair with a well-known journalist is exposed. As his wife, former popstar Betty (Janssen) learns about his infidelity, she\'s set to use all his secrets and take advantage of his weak spots to take his empire from him. Netflix Related: Best streaming services "I am beyond excited to return home to the Netherlands for my very first Dutch role!" Janssen said in a statement. "It\'s an honour to have the opportunity to work with Nico Moolenaar and the rest of this talented team. I am grateful to be back in business with Netflix once again and to be part of this truly captivating story set in the beautiful city of Amsterdam. The city that has my heart." The role of Betty was created with Janssen in mind, explained creator and executive producer Moolenaar: "It has been a long-time ambition to bring our national treasure, Famke Janssen, back to the Netherlands to see her act in a Dutch production for the first time in her illustrious career," the creator said when the series was announced. Netflix "Betty was written with Famke in mind, and I am thrilled that she\'s willing to embark on this adventure with us." Moolenar has worked with Netflix before on series Undercover and prequel movie Ferry , both starring Elise Schaap, who also features on Amsterdam Empire . "After spending years in the world of Ferry Bouwman, it is exciting to create a new universe," Moolenar said. "As always, I do this with my regular partners in crime, Piet Matthys and Bart Uytdenhouwen, on my side. I am privileged to add the wonderfully talented Jonas Govaerts to the team. Netflix Not many actors, if any, can say that they have played both a Marvel superhero and a Bond villain within their career - but Famke Janssen sure can. From breakout roles playing assassin Zenia Onatopp in 1995’s GoldenEye to her beloved run as the telepathic Jean Grey in numerous X-Men movies, Janssen, 60, has continued on to play a wide array of characters, including recently in the Taken trilogy and as Viola Davis’s longtime love interest, Eve, on Shondaland’s hit How to Get Away with Murder television series. Born in the Netherlands, Janssen is now returning to her roots on-screen for the very first time, as Betty in the new Amsterdam Empire series. Now streaming on Netflix, she plays a longtime famous European model and singer, who finds herself having to pick up the pieces of her life when her husband (played by Jacob Derwig), a Dutch coffee and cannabis mogul, leaves her for a younger woman (played by Elise Schaap). What follows is a gritty and calculating tale, with Betty striving relentlessly to get revenge on her ex. “I’m very proud of it,” Janssen told me during our recent Zoom interview for Amsterdam Empire . “This is a project that was the most different from roles I’ve had. Having agency, where I’m an executive producer. I co-designed my costumes. I’m the star. It’s been an incredible experience.” Having grown up in the Netherlands, Janssen revealed to me that she left the northwestern European country at 18 when she began her career traveling the world as a model. Those experiences ultimately brought her to New York, which is where she first began her acting career. With Amsterdam Empire , this is Janssen’s first time acting in her native Dutch language. MORE FOR YOU Famke Janssen in "Amsterdam Empire" Netflix / Mark de Blok “I associate acting with the English language. Over the years, some things had come in and it just hadn’t been right - the components weren’t all there, but I think it was the fact that Netflix was behind this and that we live in a different time now. I mean, during my years as an actor - let’s say 10-15 years ago - it was unheard of that people would watch an international series with subtitles, but streaming changed the game. It changed everything.” Janssen was adamant within her executive producer position here, that unlike with many of her previous acting jobs, that she would have an active role in crafting who Betty would be for the screen. Famke Janssen in "Amsterdam Empire" Netflix / Mark de Blok “I want to have a say over who she is, how she dresses, everything,” Janssen said. “I’m an executive producer and I’m co-designing my own costumes. I’m going to do a music video and actually sing and dance in it. It ended up being such a rich experience, which I hadn’t anticipated when I said yes to it. But ultimately, I wear so many different hats on it and I feel I’m so proud of what we accomplished and what I personally added to the series, enriching Betty as a character.” She added: “In my almost 30 years of experience as an actor, what I’ve learned is that I’ve had to fight for the characters because most of the time they were written by men. They were underwritten characters, they were one-dimensional, they were misunderstood. Then, we’re like - Alright, bring me in. The knowledge of what it’s like to be a woman, the knowledge of what it’s like to be underestimated and knowledge of all of those things put together. I really got to work with that in the most fun and exciting way on Amsterdam Empire .” Famke Janssen in "Amsterdam Empire" Netflix / Mark de Blok When it came to performing as Betty for the screen, Janssen wanted to make sure that people could understood her character’s ways and reasoning for the questionable things she does on the drama series. “The underlying pain, because honestly, I think being cheated on is one of the worst things in the world, but then to be cheated on publicly, where everyone knows about it. Whenever I read these things in the papers about people, I just so empathize with those people - like how painful that must be, you know?” Throughout the many characters Janssen has brought to the screen over the past three decades, she says she always learns something new about either herself or a character with the acting muscle that she is able to bring to each character. With Amsterdam Empire , Janssen loved how “unpredictably crazy” Betty was, which she says she could identify with, but also sees a clear contrast between herself and her new Netflix character. Famke Janssen in "Amsterdam Empire" Netflix / Mark de Blok Janssen said with Betty in mind, “I’m a very different person and she screams for attention in a way that I would never, but I do love her fashion and I’m very proud of her.” Being the seasoned actor that she is within the entertainment industry, when I asked Janssen what modern trends she is seeing that she is enjoying around the business today and if there are any parts of Hollywood from yesterday that she wishes were still in place, she referenced the films of the 1920s and 1930s, “when women were protagonists. All those comedies from that time where women were glamorous, they were funny, they were irreverent. They were the leads. Those movies were centered around these women and they were allowed to be so many things. It’s so interesting to see how we went from the 20s and 30s to now, going backwards. I’m like - Wait, why did we go in the wrong direction here? The flip side of that is in my experience in the business, is that seeing in the last 10-15 years, the strides we’ve made in diversity in film, I have to say, I find that so wonderful to see. I’m not saying we’re there yet, but I’m seeing huge strides.” Janssen also shared that when she first started acting in the U.S., all she saw were white men on film crews. “Now, you come to set and it’s just not like that anymore. So, it’s wonderful to see. I think we do have to celebrate the success in that area. I would say bring back more female-driven content.” Janssen’s performance as Jean Grey, which she was first introduced as in 2000’s X-Men , is still arguably her most iconic character to date. Having such a lasting impact on moviegoers, I wondered why Janssen believes that audiences still resonate with her superhero depiction and what it means to her to have played a character that has maintained such longevity and continues to receive vocal admiration from fans these 25 years later. Famke Janssen as Jean Grey in 2000\'s "X-Men" 20th Century Studios/Disney “It’s super flattering and wonderful.” Janssen said of her X-Men fanbase. “When I was cast as Jean Grey, not knowing anything about those comic books and then starting to read them for research and realizing - Oh, this is so interesting because this is just about a group of people who feel ostracized. They feel like outsiders. They don’t belong in the society. That’s this universal theme of how we all feel in life. We all kind of feel like we are outsiders and we don’t quite belong. I want to give credit to for Bryan Singer and the creators of the first X-Men film. The emphasis was on making these people human, with flaws and insecurities, who happen to have superpowers, rather than the other way around. So, I think that may be part of the reason for the longevity.” With the Marvel Cinematic Universe having expanded more and more over the years, including with the upcoming Avengers: Doomsday and Avengers: Secret Wars , does Janssen have any interest to reprise her Jean Grey role any time soon? “I don’t even know if that’s worth thinking about,” Janssen said, “I mean, I played her over five movies. I’m incredibly grateful for the experience. I know they brought some of the other characters back over some of the other movies. I think I’ve been so lucky in the fact that I’ve done - including The Wolverine film - I’ve been in five of them and really got to explore. Could I have explored more? Could we have explored more with Jean Grey? Yes, absolutely - and with The Phoenix, but these are big ensemble casts and there’s only so much time that we can spend on them. It’s been a wonderful experience and I just am grateful for all the time that I’ve spent.” Looking ahead, Janssen recently finished filming a movie in Arkansas and has been working on one in Bulgaria, with another project scheduled next for her in Boston. For today’s emerging young Hollywood stars who are now experiencing the joys and the downfalls that come with fame - yet unlike when Janssen was coming up in Hollywood, now adding the pressures and expectations around social media. Janssen herself has chosen against having social media, saying that she is “blissfully ignorant in that area. It feels as an outsider, I’m not on it, but it feels incredibly toxic. I don’t think I’m made for it. I think I’m too sensitive and I think it would become too time-consuming. I think it would be too destructive in my life. And so, I opted out and just do not participate in it.” Famke Janssen in "Amsterdam Empire" Netflix / Mark de Blok As for the best advice that Janssen would give to today’s rising stars? “I would say for anyone who starts as an actor is that authenticity is really the most important part. I think in the beginning of one’s career, and very much that was true for me as much as anyone else, it’s like everything that makes you different - my name, my height, my looks. Am I Russian? Am I Dutch? I don’t look American, I don’t look Dutch. That’s the part where people are like - I don’t know what to do with her . Ultimately, when you stand your ground and you go - But watch me! I am me and I am authentic and I’m going to have you catch-up to who I am, rather than conform and try to become something to fit in.” With all seven episodes of Amsterdam Empire now available to stream on Netflix, I left Janssen with my signature interview question, wondering what she would say to her character Betty, if only she could. Famke Janssen in "Amsterdam Empire" Netflix / Mark de Blok “I think that I would say - I feel you and I get you and I understand you. Betty, I really felt like she didn’t feel supported in her life. We see Betty and we know nothing about her. She doesn’t have a family, she doesn’t have a friend. She has to steal the dog, basically, to have any kind of companionship. I had to fight for her to be seen as a whole character and I’m proud of what I was able to do with what I was given, because she didn’t have a fair fight.” Editorial Standards Reprints & Permissions LOADING VIDEO PLAYER... Amsterdam Empire cast and character guide: Who plays whom in Netflix\'s latest Dutch crime drama? Discuss Now Amsterdam Empire cast and character guide (Image Via Netflix) Netflix recently premiered its new show Amsterdam Empire on 31st October, 2025. It is a Dutch crime drama that follows Betty Jonkers, once Amsterdam\'s glamorous pop star, who left her career and fame to marry the owner of a cannabis coffee shop empire, Jack van Doorn. The high-profile marriage soon struggles when Jack\'s affair with a journalist, Morjolein, comes to the surface. This led to some furious confrontation between the couple, and soon Jack reveals he is in love with Morjolein and would want a divorce. Betty then decides to rip apart Jack\'s life using her knowledge of his shady businesses and its secrets. The show comes with an exceptional list of cast members, and their power-packed performances make the show a worthwhile watch. Here is the full cast and character guide to Amsterdam Empire. Amsterdam Empire cast and character guide: Who plays whom in the latest Dutch drama explored Famke Janssen as Betty Jonkers (Image Via Netflix) Famke Janssen as Betty Jonkers Betty plays the former pop star, deeply wounded by her husband\'s betrayal. After years of being overshadowed by her husband\'s cannabis empire, she discovers his affair with a journalist, Morjolein. When Jack reveals that he wants a divorce from her, she smashes the window of her husband\'s expensive car. This becomes her breaking point after which Betty decides to destroy him piece by piece. Amsterdam Empire will be Famke Janssen\'s first Dutch-language show in decades, and for the first time, she is returning to Dutch TV after her Hollywood career. She is also the co-producer of the show and has earlier been seen in X-Men, Taken and Hemlock Grove. Jacob Derwig as Jack van Doorn (Image Via Netflix) Jacob Derwig as Jack van Doorn Jack is Betty\'s husband, who is a self-made entrepreneur building the cannabis empire named The Jackal. He thrives on control and eventually falls in love with a journalist, upsetting his wife. His wife, who also possesses all of his secrets about the shady empire, takes revenge. Jack\'s empire begins to crash as his affair comes to light while his image is shattered and replaced with criminal entanglements and a chaotic life. Jacob Derwig is one of the Netherlands’ most acclaimed actors. He has also won a Golden Calf, which is considered the Dutch equivalent of an Oscar. He shared credits in The Resistance Banker and The Judgement. Elise Schaap as Marjolein Hofman (Image Via Netflix) Elise Schaap as Marjolein Hofman Elise Schaap plays the ambitious journalist Marjolein with whom Jack had an affair and fell in love. She is the reason behind the conflict between he couple, which drives the show. She is smart and aware of the moral tightrope she is walking on. She doesn\'t embody the stereotypical home breaker personality, but chases power alongside Jack. When Betty exposes their affair, Marjolein becomes a target of both media scrutiny and Betty’s wrath. Elise Schaap is again a renowned face in television in the Netherlands\' and has previously appeared in Undercover and Ferry . Jade Olieberg as Katja van Doorn Katja is Jack’s daughter from a previous relationship. She is portrayed as a restless young woman who doesn\'t want to be involved in her father\'s business but is often dragged into it. When Betty and Jack\'s relationship strains, it affects Katja. She starts to see through her father\'s manipulation while her bond with Betty is damaged. She desires a new start for herself, but is surrounded by the chaos of the Dutch underworld. Jade, who plays Katja in Amsterdam Empire , has been seen before in the horror series Ares . Known for playing complex characters, she has also appeared in The East and Hacked . Bart Slegers as Gijs Tichelaar Gijs is Jack’s long-time business partner and enforcer. He is the man who knows every deep secret of his shady empire. He has seen Amsterdam evolve and understands every curve of the city. He is more loyal to money and profit than most people, and eventually, when Betty begins to dismantle it, he becomes the protector of the empire. His loyalty, like the city’s underworld, comes at a price. Wondering where you have seen Bart Slegers before. He is literally the powerhouse of Dutch cinema and theatre, known for his award-winning role in Son of Mine, before appearing on Amsterdam Empire. By Sirena He Published: Nov 25, 2025 5:09 PM EST What does it mean to be an icon? Nowadays, people throw around the word as loosely as an Instagram comment. If you ask Famke Janssen, star of the 1995 James Bond film GoldenEye , icon status is a mindset. “This is how I\'ve lived my entire life," Janssen tells me over Zoom. "I do things before I even know if I\'m ready to do them. Just go for broke and throw myself in head first. See if I survive and come out okay on the other side." After three decades in the film industry, it\'s worked out great so far. In GoldenEye —which celebrates its 30th anniversary this month—Janssen debuted as an original Bond girl named Xenia Onatopp. (Pun very much intended.) You may remember her as the villain who squeezes her rivals to death with her thighs. "When I saw the name of my character, Xenia Onatopp, I thought, T his is what I\'ve loved about the Bond franchise ," says Janssen. "The tongue in cheek sense of humor in it." Janssen originally took Onatopp\'s name as a challenge. She wanted to push her character to the limits of what people have come to expect from Bond girls. The actress didn\'t want to be another femme fatale, seductress, or action star, yet Janssen still managed to be all that and more in GoldenEye. She sought to take a bite out of the role and leave a mark on it that would stay with the audience. For many fans, Onatopp may have even been their sexual awakening. "In hindsight, it\'s pretty brave that, as a young actress with very little experience in such a big franchise, I dared to take those big risks," she says now. "I\'m proud of that." Janssen could have built on her Onatopp fame and played out the Bond girl trope, but she wanted more. After GoldenEye , Janssen went on to star as Marvel ’s first live-action version of Jean Grey in a trilogy of X-Men films. She appeared in three Taken films with Liam Neeson, and she made her directorial debut with 2011\'s Bringing Up Bobby. Janssen tells me, "I\'ve earned my stripes now." Just last month, Janssen released her first series in her native Dutch—a Netflix crime drama that she executive produced and starred in called Amsterdam Empire . In the seven-episode series, Janssen plays Betty Jonker, a former \'90s pop star who is unceremoniously dumped by her drug kingpin husband. Janssen tells me that she learned to dance and sing for the role, which came easily to her. "I feel incredibly young and I have a ton of energy," Janssen says. "I feel we\'re all ageless in a way." Below, Janssen looks back on thirty years of GoldenEye , reveals that she broke her rib while filming a fight scene with Pierce Brosnan, and shares her hope for the franchise\'s first female Bond. Keith Hamshere // Getty Images Pierce Brosnan starring as James Bond for the first time along with Famke Janssen as Xenia Onatopp This interview has been edited and condensed for clarity. ESQUIRE: What were feeling at the time when you heard you landed the role of Xenia Onatopp in GoldenEye ? FAMKE JANSSEN: I was filming another movie called Lord of Illusions (1995) at the time. It was the same studio that was making Bond, and some of the people working on Bond had seen my performance. I was asked to audition, and then I ultimately became one of three actresses, who screen tested opposite Pierce Brosnan in London. It was an incredible opportunity and it opened so many doors for me. It was fairly early on in my career. I\'d done a few films [for TV], but nothing on that scale. It really put me in the spotlight in a way that I hadn\'t been as an actor yet. I was a model before, so I\'d had a lot of attention in that field. It was a little scary. So many people were going to watch that film. There hadn\'t been a Bond in many years, and Pierce was the first to restart the series. All eyes were on the franchise. So I worked very hard to make that character as memorable as possible. Keith Hamshere // Getty Images Famke Janssen broke a rib in her grappling scene with Pierce Brosnan. Xenia is so iconic in GoldenEye . She\'s the ultimate female James Bond villain. What do you make of the character\'s legacy after thirty years? There\'s an unpredictability that I want to bring to my characters. At the time, I was so aware of the stereotypes that came with being female in a Bond movie. I watched all those older Bond movies to see how the previous characters had been portrayed. As a strong woman who has grown up in a household full of women, I was raised to believe that we\'re equal and we should fight for things. I wanted to go all the way. Xenia Onatopp is a very physical character. Did you enjoy doing all the stunts in the movie? Yes, I enjoy being trained for something in a movie, no matter what it is. Whether it\'s horseback riding or gun training, I\'m learning new things. It\'s an added, exhilarating bonus to what I do. Usually, I try to do as much as they allow me to do. There are certain stunts that they don\'t allow you to do because they\'re too risky, and you have to be back on set the next day in one piece. Is it true that you broke a rib while filming the steam room scene with Pierce Brosnan? In that fight scene, they padded the walls. Since Pierce was throwing me against the wall a lot, he was being very gentle with me. I thought, It\'s going to be hard for me to act out that fight unless he actually throws me up against the wall . So I said, "Pierce, the walls are padded. Just really throw me." Then, I ended up breaking a rib. [Laughs.] But that\'s not the first time. I also broke a rib during Hansel and Gretel: Witch Hunters . When you literally throw yourself into your characters and you are willing to take risks and do stunts, that\'s something that can happen—and I\'m okay with it. Would you want to see a female James Bond in the franchise? I\'m glad that conversation is finally happening. I\'ve always said it. I\'ve advocated for it since I appeared in GoldenEye . It\'s a franchise that has been around for sixty years. They\'ve reinvented themselves many times. I would love to see a Bond movie with a female Bond. It would be absolutely amazing. I imagine that a lot of women would feel the same way and, probably, men too. netflix Janssen as Betty Jonkers in Amsterdam Empire. Your new Netflix series, Amsterdam Empire , is so much fun. What was it like being an executive producer on a show where you\'re also the lead actress? I\'m so grateful for my experiences over the years. I\'ve never publicized myself as much as other people have. Sometimes, I\'ve opted to do smaller parts and made the choice to be a little less visible to work on my craft more. The fact that I am still around after all these years—and having done eighty projects at this point in my life—I thought, I should be able to be an executive producer on a project . I like the character, but I wanted to have more of a say in her journey, in the character development, and in the script. I even ended up designing my own costumes. One of the costumes, the red cape, is actually modeled after a vintage cape I own. I brought it in and said "Let\'s make this one in different colors." It was so much a part of Betty\'s personality, because she\'s so colorful as a character. I wanted those colors reflected in her wardrobe. Betty\'s story in Amsterdam Empire is so empowering. She\'s getting divorced and her career is behind her. A lot of the time society would tell you that as a woman, your life is kind of valueless at this point, but her life is still an adventure. What was that like to portray? Age is not something I ever think about, because I feel incredibly young. Betty is a ball of energy that had so much potential, like a missile. If she wasn\'t directed in the right way, she could be highly destructive. But if she put it towards something good, she would be a force to be reckoned with. I recognize that a little bit in myself, too. I did something for the first time before for this role—singing and dancing for a music video. It was one of the best experiences I\'ve ever had in my life. It was not an easy assignment, because the character is meant to be at least twenty years younger than she is in present time. You can\'t dance younger. You just have to work harder to pull it off. Every free moment, I was either in the dance studio with my choreographer or in the vocal booth with my vocal coach. The day that we filmed the music video last year, which was two or three days after my birthday, I just cried at the end—tears of joy and sadness all at the same time—because it had been such a beautiful experience. You\'ve lived your life with so much grace and passion. It\'s empowering to see. Thank you. You have to keep going and be a role model for all other women out there. That\'s all we can do. By George Lewis Published: 03 November 2025 We may be accustomed to comebacks in the Marvel Cinematic Universe , with several big names returning to old roles. It\'s no different for some of the stars from the X-Men franchise — but not all of them. Famke Janssen, who portrayed Jean Grey/Phoenix in four films across the series over a 14-year period, has confirmed she hasn\'t been asked to reprise her role since Marvel acquired the rights to the characters. "Never. Never ever," she told Entertainment Weekly . "Every time I do an interview, it\'s mentioned. It\'s interesting. I didn\'t realise that was such a big part. Every interview I do, that will come up. "I should be flattered, I suppose, that this character has resonated with people. It\'s been so long, but it\'s nice that people are still talking about her. I\'m sure every single time there\'s a new [film] that they\'re doing, like Avengers: Doomsday , it\'ll come up again." What to Read Next While it doesn\'t appear that Janssen will be in the fifth film in the Avengers series , there are several X-Men stars returning. Kelsey Grammer, Patrick Stewart, Ian McKellen, Alan Cumming, James Marsden and Rebecca Romijn are all reprising their respective roles. Despite the positive critical reception and whopping commercial success, it\'s currently unclear if Wolverine will be part of Avengers: Doomsday . Jackman certainly wasn\'t letting anything slip when speaking on The View in June. Aside from the slew of X-Men stars, the cast for Avengers: Doomsday is stacked, with Florence Pugh, Sebastian Stan, Robert Downey Jr, Chris Hemsworth, Vanessa Kirby, Pedro Pascal, Joseph Quinn and Anthony Mackie all set to appear. The next two Avengers movies will set up Doctor Doom as the next big bad as heroes from different Earths arrive in the Marvel Cinematic Universe, and fans can finally see the Fox heroes from the X-Men and Fantastic Four meeting up with the MCU Avengers for what should be a fun crossover battle. Names like Patrick Stewart, Ian McKellen, James Marsden, Kelsey Grammer, Alan Cumming, and Rebecca Romijn are all confirmed to appear. However, one other original X-Men actor said they won’t be back. Videos by ComicBook.com In a recent interview with Kristian Harloff , Famke Janssen discussed her past movies and what was coming next for her career, including her new Netflix series, Amsterdam Empire . In the interview, Harloff asked if Janssen had been asked to return for Avengers: Doomsday , and she admitted that she is not returning and wasn’t interested in the opportunity. She said that she is an executive producer on Amsterdam Empire and has a seat at the table where she has a say in things that need to be changed. “I would not be asked back on Doomsday , or somewhere else, with that type of input. That’s not what they want from me,” she admitted. Janssen also said that she prefers not to look back and wants to keep moving forward in her career. “It’s hard for me now to just look back and worry, or think about a part where I get a few lines,” she said. “It just doesn’t seem that interesting to me. I’m in a different place, and I’ve earned my way into this moment, and I’m running with it, because this is 80 films under my belt, and I’ve paid my dues . “ However, Famke Janssen admitted that she isn’t opposed to doing something like Avengers: Doomsday , where she would be part of a fun ensemble. “But at this moment in time, I just finished a movie yesterday in Bulgaria, called One Second After , and I also designed my clothes on that one as well,” she admitted. “It’s so cool to have these added parts to it, what I’m doing in my life right now, because I love creativity. I’m always looking to create.” Read Next Avengers: Doomsday Shows How Much the MCU’s Power Level Has Changed (& It’s a Problem) Famke Janssen Skipping Avengers: Doomsday Is Best For Both Parties Image Courtesy of Fox Famke Janssen was solid as Jean Grey in X-Men, but honestly, it is better for her to remain away from Avengers: Doomsday for a couple of important reasons. First, as Janssen said, she has become more of a player with a seat at the table on her recent projects. While it might be fun to come back in a nostalgic role, it isn’t the best thing for her right now as she continues to find her place as a veteran actor. However, even more important is the fact that this movie is going to have way too many heroes showing up anyway. Why would someone who is finally gaining respect behind the scenes want to come back for what would likely be a performance with a couple of lines, and then possibly get killed off by the end? Janssen finished her role as Jean Grey by dying in X-Men: The Last Stand , and honestly, it might be better to bring back Sophie Turner as Jean Grey since she showed she survived in her world in Dark Phoenix . The fact that the original X-Men are all that has been advertised is telling, and at their ages, it is almost assured they will not last to the reboot following Avengers: Secret Wars . New X-Men heroes need to emerge to carry on that role, and Famke Janssen’s Jean Grey is part of an era that has already moved on. Also, remember, Jean Grey killed Cyclops in X-Men: The Last Stand . Since James Marsden is returning, it proves that this isn’t the world that Jean died on, so it is likely better not to bring Janssen back, considering the confusion it could cause mainstream fans when the X-Men step into the MCU for the first time. Famke presented an award at the prestigious event, amid a career resurgence for the Dutch native. She recently starred in the Netflix series Amsterdam Empire , which was released in October, marking the first time she has appeared in a production in her home country of the Netherlands. Watch the trailer for Amsterdam Empire below... WATCH: The trailer for Netflix’s Amsterdam Empire You may also like Famke Janssen makes red carpet appearance 30 years after Bond The synopsis for the show reads: "Jack van Doorn, the rich and notorious founder of the coffee shop empire Jackal, has had to fight his entire career against criminals, competitors, and absurd Dutch laws to become the biggest of them all." "When his affair with a well-known journalist comes to light, it turns out that his most dangerous enemy has been living under his roof all this time: his betrayed wife, Betty, an ex-pop diva who knows all his weak spots and secrets and will not rest until she has taken everything from him." © Getty Images The actress presented at the prestigious event Famke, a former model, is best known for her roles in the Bond flick GoldenEye , the Taken franchise and as Jean Grey in X-Men . She starred alongside Pierce Brosnan in the 1995 Bond film as Xenia Onatopp , a fighter pilot and assassin who became one of the most iconic villains in the franchise. Famke spoke to The Guardian about her star-making turn in the flick, sharing that she put her all into the role. "I was very aware of the pitfalls of being a model-turned-actor-turned-Bond girl. I thought \'Bond girl\' was such a demeaning term," she explained. © Netflix / Mark de Blok Famke stars in Amsterdam Empire "But I thought: \'I have nothing to lose; if I do this, I\'m going to go all the way.\' So I came up with a lot of the things that are now in the film, because I wanted to make a memorable character, not play her the way she was written." "I grew up on Bond movies, because my dad used to like them, and so I always thought of them as comedies, as tongue-in-cheek," she added. "I thought: \'Let me make this character unforgettable.\' I went for broke. It easily could have failed. I don\'t know where I got the confidence." She portrayed Xenia Onatopp in GoldenEye The brunette beauty shared her take on the new direction of the Bond franchise, following Amazon MGM Studio\'s announcement that it would be taking creative control of 007 after longtime producers Michael G. Wilson and Barbara Broccoli chose to step away. "I hope that there are more female villains, because they are fantastic characters," Famke told Variety following the announcement. "We\'ve seen the franchise have a lot of interesting characters over the past 60 years, and I\'m curious to see what they do next." © Getty Images She starred alongside Pierce Brosnan in the flick "They\'ve been so clever at reinventing themselves over and over again to remain relevant. I\'m very much looking forward to [seeing] who is going to play Bond, who else is going to be cast in it, what the storyline is, and what exotic locations they go to." She added that it was important for the next Bond girl to "be authentically yourself" and not "think about the people who\'ve played those parts before or the pressures that come with playing it". By Stefania Sarrubba Published: 30 October 2025 Netflix Netflix might\'ve just dropped your next binge watch with Dutch crime drama Amsterdam Empire , starring Famke Janssen as a woman hellbent on revenge. Announced last year as a "captivating" crime series set in the coffee shops of the Dutch capital, Amsterdam Empire is now available to stream on Netflix. Created by Nico Moolenaar, Bart Uytdenhouwen and Piet Matthys, the seven-part crime drama stars Jacob Derwig as Jack van Doorn, the founder of coffeeshop empire The Jackal. What to Read Next Jack has become rich and famous by fighting off criminals, competitors and Dutch laws, but his empire is threatened when his affair with a well-known journalist is exposed. As his wife, former popstar Betty (Janssen) learns about his infidelity, she\'s set to use all his secrets and take advantage of his weak spots to take his empire from him. Netflix Related: Best streaming services "I am beyond excited to return home to the Netherlands for my very first Dutch role!" Janssen said in a statement. "It\'s an honour to have the opportunity to work with Nico Moolenaar and the rest of this talented team. I am grateful to be back in business with Netflix once again and to be part of this truly captivating story set in the beautiful city of Amsterdam. The city that has my heart." The role of Betty was created with Janssen in mind, explained creator and executive producer Moolenaar: "It has been a long-time ambition to bring our national treasure, Famke Janssen, back to the Netherlands to see her act in a Dutch production for the first time in her illustrious career," the creator said when the series was announced. Netflix "Betty was written with Famke in mind, and I am thrilled that she\'s willing to embark on this adventure with us." Moolenar has worked with Netflix before on series Undercover and prequel movie Ferry , both starring Elise Schaap, who also features on Amsterdam Empire . "After spending years in the world of Ferry Bouwman, it is exciting to create a new universe," Moolenar said. "As always, I do this with my regular partners in crime, Piet Matthys and Bart Uytdenhouwen, on my side. I am privileged to add the wonderfully talented Jonas Govaerts to the team. Please stay tuned for more updates as we assemble a stellar cast and crew." Released today, Amsterdam Empire also stars Jade Olieberg as Katja van Doorn, Yannick van de Velde as Erik Ketels, and Jesse Mensah as Patrick van Doorn. Amsterdam Empire is streaming on Netflix. Netflix Not many actors, if any, can say that they have played both a Marvel superhero and a Bond villain within their career - but Famke Janssen sure can. From breakout roles playing assassin Zenia Onatopp in 1995’s GoldenEye to her beloved run as the telepathic Jean Grey in numerous X-Men movies, Janssen, 60, has continued on to play a wide array of characters, including recently in the Taken trilogy and as Viola Davis’s longtime love interest, Eve, on Shondaland’s hit How to Get Away with Murder television series. Born in the Netherlands, Janssen is now returning to her roots on-screen for the very first time, as Betty in the new Amsterdam Empire series. Now streaming on Netflix, she plays a longtime famous European model and singer, who finds herself having to pick up the pieces of her life when her husband (played by Jacob Derwig), a Dutch coffee and cannabis mogul, leaves her for a younger woman (played by Elise Schaap). What follows is a gritty and calculating tale, with Betty striving relentlessly to get revenge on her ex. “I’m very proud of it,” Janssen told me during our recent Zoom interview for Amsterdam Empire . “This is a project that was the most different from roles I’ve had. Having agency, where I’m an executive producer. I co-designed my costumes. I’m the star. It’s been an incredible experience.” Having grown up in the Netherlands, Janssen revealed to me that she left the northwestern European country at 18 when she began her career traveling the world as a model. Those experiences ultimately brought her to New York, which is where she first began her acting career. With Amsterdam Empire , this is Janssen’s first time acting in her native Dutch language. MORE FOR YOU Famke Janssen in "Amsterdam Empire" Netflix / Mark de Blok “I associate acting with the English language. Over the years, some things had come in and it just hadn’t been right - the components weren’t all there, but I think it was the fact that Netflix was behind this and that we live in a different time now. I mean, during my years as an actor - let’s say 10-15 years ago - it was unheard of that people would watch an international series with subtitles, but streaming changed the game. It changed everything.” Janssen was adamant within her executive producer position here, that unlike with many of her previous acting jobs, that she would have an active role in crafting who Betty would be for the screen. Famke Janssen in "Amsterdam Empire" Netflix / Mark de Blok “I want to have a say over who she is, how she dresses, everything,” Janssen said. “I’m an executive producer and I’m co-designing my own costumes. I’m going to do a music video and actually sing and dance in it. It ended up being such a rich experience, which I hadn’t anticipated when I said yes to it. But ultimately, I wear so many different hats on it and I feel I’m so proud of what we accomplished and what I personally added to the series, enriching Betty as a character.” She added: “In my almost 30 years of experience as an actor, what I’ve learned is that I’ve had to fight for the characters because most of the time they were written by men. They were underwritten characters, they were one-dimensional, they were misunderstood. Then, we’re like - Alright, bring me in. The knowledge of what it’s like to be a woman, the knowledge of what it’s like to be underestimated and knowledge of all of those things put together. I really got to work with that in the most fun and exciting way on Amsterdam Empire .” Famke Janssen in "Amsterdam Empire" Netflix / Mark de Blok When it came to performing as Betty for the screen, Janssen wanted to make sure that people could understood her character’s ways and reasoning for the questionable things she does on the drama series. “The underlying pain, because honestly, I think being cheated on is one of the worst things in the world, but then to be cheated on publicly, where everyone knows about it. Whenever I read these things in the papers about people, I just so empathize with those people - like how painful that must be, you know?” Throughout the many characters Janssen has brought to the screen over the past three decades, she says she always learns something new about either herself or a character with the acting muscle that she is able to bring to each character. With Amsterdam Empire , Janssen loved how “unpredictably crazy” Betty was, which she says she could identify with, but also sees a clear contrast between herself and her new Netflix character. Famke Janssen in "Amsterdam Empire" Netflix / Mark de Blok Janssen said with Betty in mind, “I’m a very different person and she screams for attention in a way that I would never, but I do love her fashion and I’m very proud of her.” Being the seasoned actor that she is within the entertainment industry, when I asked Janssen what modern trends she is seeing that she is enjoying around the business today and if there are any parts of Hollywood from yesterday that she wishes were still in place, she referenced the films of the 1920s and 1930s, “when women were protagonists. All those comedies from that time where women were glamorous, they were funny, they were irreverent. They were the leads. Those movies were centered around these women and they were allowed to be so many things. It’s so interesting to see how we went from the 20s and 30s to now, going backwards. I’m like - Wait, why did we go in the wrong direction here? The flip side of that is in my experience in the business, is that seeing in the last 10-15 years, the strides we’ve made in diversity in film, I have to say, I find that so wonderful to see. I’m not saying we’re there yet, but I’m seeing huge strides.” Janssen also shared that when she first started acting in the U.S., all she saw were white men on film crews. “Now, you come to set and it’s just not like that anymore. So, it’s wonderful to see. I think we do have to celebrate the success in that area. I would say bring back more female-driven content.” Janssen’s performance as Jean Grey, which she was first introduced as in 2000’s X-Men , is still arguably her most iconic character to date. Having such a lasting impact on moviegoers, I wondered why Janssen believes that audiences still resonate with her superhero depiction and what it means to her to have played a character that has maintained such longevity and continues to receive vocal admiration from fans these 25 years later. Famke Janssen as Jean Grey in 2000\'s "X-Men" 20th Century Studios/Disney “It’s super flattering and wonderful.” Janssen said of her X-Men fanbase. “When I was cast as Jean Grey, not knowing anything about those comic books and then starting to read them for research and realizing - Oh, this is so interesting because this is just about a group of people who feel ostracized. They feel like outsiders. They don’t belong in the society. That’s this universal theme of how we all feel in life. We all kind of feel like we are outsiders and we don’t quite belong. I want to give credit to for Bryan Singer and the creators of the first X-Men film. The emphasis was on making these people human, with flaws and insecurities, who happen to have superpowers, rather than the other way around. So, I think that may be part of the reason for the longevity.” With the Marvel Cinematic Universe having expanded more and more over the years, including with the upcoming Avengers: Doomsday and Avengers: Secret Wars , does Janssen have any interest to reprise her Jean Grey role any time soon? “I don’t even know if that’s worth thinking about,” Janssen said, “I mean, I played her over five movies. I’m incredibly grateful for the experience. I know they brought some of the other characters back over some of the other movies. I think I’ve been so lucky in the fact that I’ve done - including The Wolverine film - I’ve been in five of them and really got to explore. Could I have explored more? Could we have explored more with Jean Grey? Yes, absolutely - and with The Phoenix, but these are big ensemble casts and there’s only so much time that we can spend on them. It’s been a wonderful experience and I just am grateful for all the time that I’ve spent.” Looking ahead, Janssen recently finished filming a movie in Arkansas and has been working on one in Bulgaria, with another project scheduled next for her in Boston. For today’s emerging young Hollywood stars who are now experiencing the joys and the downfalls that come with fame - yet unlike when Janssen was coming up in Hollywood, now adding the pressures and expectations around social media. Janssen herself has chosen against having social media, saying that she is “blissfully ignorant in that area. It feels as an outsider, I’m not on it, but it feels incredibly toxic. I don’t think I’m made for it. I think I’m too sensitive and I think it would become too time-consuming. I think it would be too destructive in my life. And so, I opted out and just do not participate in it.” Famke Janssen in "Amsterdam Empire" Netflix / Mark de Blok As for the best advice that Janssen would give to today’s rising stars? “I would say for anyone who starts as an actor is that authenticity is really the most important part. I think in the beginning of one’s career, and very much that was true for me as much as anyone else, it’s like everything that makes you different - my name, my height, my looks. Am I Russian? Am I Dutch? I don’t look American, I don’t look Dutch. That’s the part where people are like - I don’t know what to do with her . Ultimately, when you stand your ground and you go - But watch me! I am me and I am authentic and I’m going to have you catch-up to who I am, rather than conform and try to become something to fit in.” With all seven episodes of Amsterdam Empire now available to stream on Netflix, I left Janssen with my signature interview question, wondering what she would say to her character Betty, if only she could. Famke Janssen in "Amsterdam Empire" Netflix / Mark de Blok “I think that I would say - I feel you and I get you and I understand you. Betty, I really felt like she didn’t feel supported in her life. We see Betty and we know nothing about her. She doesn’t have a family, she doesn’t have a friend. She has to steal the dog, basically, to have any kind of companionship. I had to fight for her to be seen as a whole character and I’m proud of what I was able to do with what I was given, because she didn’t have a fair fight.” Editorial Standards Reprints & Permissions LOADING VIDEO PLAYER... Amsterdam Empire cast and character guide: Who plays whom in Netflix\'s latest Dutch crime drama? Discuss Now Amsterdam Empire cast and character guide (Image Via Netflix) Netflix recently premiered its new show Amsterdam Empire on 31st October, 2025. It is a Dutch crime drama that follows Betty Jonkers, once Amsterdam\'s glamorous pop star, who left her career and fame to marry the owner of a cannabis coffee shop empire, Jack van Doorn. The high-profile marriage soon struggles when Jack\'s affair with a journalist, Morjolein, comes to the surface. This led to some furious confrontation between the couple, and soon Jack reveals he is in love with Morjolein and would want a divorce. Betty then decides to rip apart Jack\'s life using her knowledge of his shady businesses and its secrets. The show comes with an exceptional list of cast members, and their power-packed performances make the show a worthwhile watch. Here is the full cast and character guide to Amsterdam Empire. Amsterdam Empire cast and character guide: Who plays whom in the latest Dutch drama explored Famke Janssen as Betty Jonkers (Image Via Netflix) Famke Janssen as Betty Jonkers Betty plays the former pop star, deeply wounded by her husband\'s betrayal. After years of being overshadowed by her husband\'s cannabis empire, she discovers his affair with a journalist, Morjolein. When Jack reveals that he wants a divorce from her, she smashes the window of her husband\'s expensive car. This becomes her breaking point after which Betty decides to destroy him piece by piece. Amsterdam Empire will be Famke Janssen\'s first Dutch-language show in decades, and for the first time, she is returning to Dutch TV after her Hollywood career. She is also the co-producer of the show and has earlier been seen in X-Men, Taken and Hemlock Grove. Jacob Derwig as Jack van Doorn (Image Via Netflix) Jacob Derwig as Jack van Doorn Jack is Betty\'s husband, who is a self-made entrepreneur building the cannabis empire named The Jackal. He thrives on control and eventually falls in love with a journalist, upsetting his wife. His wife, who also possesses all of his secrets about the shady empire, takes revenge. Jack\'s empire begins to crash as his affair comes to light while his image is shattered and replaced with criminal entanglements and a chaotic life. Jacob Derwig is one of the Netherlands’ most acclaimed actors. He has also won a Golden Calf, which is considered the Dutch equivalent of an Oscar. He shared credits in The Resistance Banker and The Judgement. Elise Schaap as Marjolein Hofman (Image Via Netflix) Elise Schaap as Marjolein Hofman Elise Schaap plays the ambitious journalist Marjolein with whom Jack had an affair and fell in love. She is the reason behind the conflict between he couple, which drives the show. She is smart and aware of the moral tightrope she is walking on. She doesn\'t embody the stereotypical home breaker personality, but chases power alongside Jack. When Betty exposes their affair, Marjolein becomes a target of both media scrutiny and Betty’s wrath. Elise Schaap is again a renowned face in television in the Netherlands\' and has previously appeared in Undercover and Ferry . Jade Olieberg as Katja van Doorn Katja is Jack’s daughter from a previous relationship. She is portrayed as a restless young woman who doesn\'t want to be involved in her father\'s business but is often dragged into it. When Betty and Jack\'s relationship strains, it affects Katja. She starts to see through her father\'s manipulation while her bond with Betty is damaged. She desires a new start for herself, but is surrounded by the chaos of the Dutch underworld. Jade, who plays Katja in Amsterdam Empire , has been seen before in the horror series Ares . Known for playing complex characters, she has also appeared in The East and Hacked . Bart Slegers as Gijs Tichelaar Gijs is Jack’s long-time business partner and enforcer. He is the man who knows every deep secret of his shady empire. He has seen Amsterdam evolve and understands every curve of the city. He is more loyal to money and profit than most people, and eventually, when Betty begins to dismantle it, he becomes the protector of the empire. His loyalty, like the city’s underworld, comes at a price. Wondering where you have seen Bart Slegers before. He is literally the powerhouse of Dutch cinema and theatre, known for his award-winning role in Son of Mine, before appearing on Amsterdam Empire. By Sirena He Published: Nov 25, 2025 5:09 PM EST What does it mean to be an icon? Nowadays, people throw around the word as loosely as an Instagram comment. If you ask Famke Janssen, star of the 1995 James Bond film GoldenEye , icon status is a mindset. “This is how I\'ve lived my entire life," Janssen tells me over Zoom. "I do things before I even know if I\'m ready to do them. Just go for broke and throw myself in head first. See if I survive and come out okay on the other side." After three decades in the film industry, it\'s worked out great so far. In GoldenEye —which celebrates its 30th anniversary this month—Janssen debuted as an original Bond girl named Xenia Onatopp. (Pun very much intended.) You may remember her as the villain who squeezes her rivals to death with her thighs. "When I saw the name of my character, Xenia Onatopp, I thought, T his is what I\'ve loved about the Bond franchise ," says Janssen. "The tongue in cheek sense of humor in it." Janssen originally took Onatopp\'s name as a challenge. She wanted to push her character to the limits of what people have come to expect from Bond girls. The actress didn\'t want to be another femme fatale, seductress, or action star, yet Janssen still managed to be all that and more in GoldenEye. She sought to take a bite out of the role and leave a mark on it that would stay with the audience. For many fans, Onatopp may have even been their sexual awakening. "In hindsight, it\'s pretty brave that, as a young actress with very little experience in such a big franchise, I dared to take those big risks," she says now. "I\'m proud of that." Janssen could have built on her Onatopp fame and played out the Bond girl trope, but she wanted more. After GoldenEye , Janssen went on to star as Marvel ’s first live-action version of Jean Grey in a trilogy of X-Men films. She appeared in three Taken films with Liam Neeson, and she made her directorial debut with 2011\'s Bringing Up Bobby. Janssen tells me, "I\'ve earned my stripes now." Just last month, Janssen released her first series in her native Dutch—a Netflix crime drama that she executive produced and starred in called Amsterdam Empire . In the seven-episode series, Janssen plays Betty Jonker, a former \'90s pop star who is unceremoniously dumped by her drug kingpin husband. Janssen tells me that she learned to dance and sing for the role, which came easily to her. "I feel incredibly young and I have a ton of energy," Janssen says. "I feel we\'re all ageless in a way." Below, Janssen looks back on thirty years of GoldenEye , reveals that she broke her rib while filming a fight scene with Pierce Brosnan, and shares her hope for the franchise\'s first female Bond. Keith Hamshere // Getty Images Pierce Brosnan starring as James Bond for the first time along with Famke Janssen as Xenia Onatopp This interview has been edited and condensed for clarity. ESQUIRE: What were feeling at the time when you heard you landed the role of Xenia Onatopp in GoldenEye ? FAMKE JANSSEN: I was filming another movie called Lord of Illusions (1995) at the time. It was the same studio that was making Bond, and some of the people working on Bond had seen my performance. I was asked to audition, and then I ultimately became one of three actresses, who screen tested opposite Pierce Brosnan in London. It was an incredible opportunity and it opened so many doors for me. It was fairly early on in my career. I\'d done a few films [for TV], but nothing on that scale. It really put me in the spotlight in a way that I hadn\'t been as an actor yet. I was a model before, so I\'d had a lot of attention in that field. It was a little scary. So many people were going to watch that film. There hadn\'t been a Bond in many years, and Pierce was the first to restart the series. All eyes were on the franchise. So I worked very hard to make that character as memorable as possible. Keith Hamshere // Getty Images Famke Janssen broke a rib in her grappling scene with Pierce Brosnan. Xenia is so iconic in GoldenEye . She\'s the ultimate female James Bond villain. What do you make of the character\'s legacy after thirty years? There\'s an unpredictability that I want to bring to my characters. At the time, I was so aware of the stereotypes that came with being female in a Bond movie. I watched all those older Bond movies to see how the previous characters had been portrayed. As a strong woman who has grown up in a household full of women, I was raised to believe that we\'re equal and we should fight for things. I wanted to go all the way. Xenia Onatopp is a very physical character. Did you enjoy doing all the stunts in the movie? Yes, I enjoy being trained for something in a movie, no matter what it is. Whether it\'s horseback riding or gun training, I\'m learning new things. It\'s an added, exhilarating bonus to what I do. Usually, I try to do as much as they allow me to do. There are certain stunts that they don\'t allow you to do because they\'re too risky, and you have to be back on set the next day in one piece. Is it true that you broke a rib while filming the steam room scene with Pierce Brosnan? In that fight scene, they padded the walls. Since Pierce was throwing me against the wall a lot, he was being very gentle with me. I thought, It\'s going to be hard for me to act out that fight unless he actually throws me up against the wall . So I said, "Pierce, the walls are padded. Just really throw me." Then, I ended up breaking a rib. [Laughs.] But that\'s not the first time. I also broke a rib during Hansel and Gretel: Witch Hunters . When you literally throw yourself into your characters and you are willing to take risks and do stunts, that\'s something that can happen—and I\'m okay with it. Would you want to see a female James Bond in the franchise? I\'m glad that conversation is finally happening. I\'ve always said it. I\'ve advocated for it since I appeared in GoldenEye . It\'s a franchise that has been around for sixty years. They\'ve reinvented themselves many times. I would love to see a Bond movie with a female Bond. It would be absolutely amazing. I imagine that a lot of women would feel the same way and, probably, men too. netflix Janssen as Betty Jonkers in Amsterdam Empire. Your new Netflix series, Amsterdam Empire , is so much fun. What was it like being an executive producer on a show where you\'re also the lead actress? I\'m so grateful for my experiences over the years. I\'ve never publicized myself as much as other people have. Sometimes, I\'ve opted to do smaller parts and made the choice to be a little less visible to work on my craft more. The fact that I am still around after all these years—and having done eighty projects at this point in my life—I thought, I should be able to be an executive producer on a project . I like the character, but I wanted to have more of a say in her journey, in the character development, and in the script. I even ended up designing my own costumes. One of the costumes, the red cape, is actually modeled after a vintage cape I own. I brought it in and said "Let\'s make this one in different colors." It was so much a part of Betty\'s personality, because she\'s so colorful as a character. I wanted those colors reflected in her wardrobe. Betty\'s story in Amsterdam Empire is so empowering. She\'s getting divorced and her career is behind her. A lot of the time society would tell you that as a woman, your life is kind of valueless at this point, but her life is still an adventure. What was that like to portray? Age is not something I ever think about, because I feel incredibly young. Betty is a ball of energy that had so much potential, like a missile. If she wasn\'t directed in the right way, she could be highly destructive. But if she put it towards something good, she would be a force to be reckoned with. I recognize that a little bit in myself, too. I did something for the first time before for this role—singing and dancing for a music video. It was one of the best experiences I\'ve ever had in my life. It was not an easy assignment, because the character is meant to be at least twenty years younger than she is in present time. You can\'t dance younger. You just have to work harder to pull it off. Every free moment, I was either in the dance studio with my choreographer or in the vocal booth with my vocal coach. The day that we filmed the music video last year, which was two or three days after my birthday, I just cried at the end—tears of joy and sadness all at the same time—because it had been such a beautiful experience. You\'ve lived your life with so much grace and passion. It\'s empowering to see. Thank you. You have to keep going and be a role model for all other women out there. That\'s all we can do. Vogue Vogue World went to Hollywood this past weekend to honor some of the showtime greats in a giant runway show at the Paramount Pictures Studios in Los Angeles, CA. Over the past two weeks, the world has mourned the untimely loss of Diane Keaton, and there was no more apt place to celebrate her iconic style . Model Betsy Gaghan was chosen to embody the actress, walking the runway dressed in a Ralph Lauren recreation of the famous “Annie Hall” look. In this past weekend’s show, she wore a white button-down shirt with oversized khaki pants, a polka dot tie around her neck, beneath a dark suit vest with a single button fastened. 5 Wearing a Ralph Lauren re-creation of the star’s iconic look, the model ambled down the runway just as Annie Hall once would have. Alamy Stock Photo Looking around the crowd as she walked, just as starry-eyed as Annie Hall herself, Gaghan’s look was finished off with a wide-brimmed hat and raffia tote, tennis racket pocking out from the inside. Ralph Lauren is habitually credited with creating Keaton’s on-screen look, though even the designer himself is quick to point out that the style was all Keaton’s own. “I’m often credited with dressing Diane in her Oscar-winning role in ‘Annie Hall,’” Lauren wrote in Keaton’s book “Fashion First,” adding, “That’s not true. Annie’s style was Diane’s style.” Any view of the late actress’ own wardrobe throughout her life would support that, for not only “Annie Hall,” but also many of her other on-screen personas. Keaton was such a style icon in life that her wardrobe permeated nearly everything she touched. 5 Much of Keaton’s “Annie Hall” wardrobe was designed by Ralph Lauren, but the styling was all her own. Courtesy Everett Collection 5 The styles of Hall and Keaton were forever enmeshed, with one drawing inspiration from the other. Getty Images As such, director Woody Allen asked her to dress herself for “Annie Hall,” knowing her true genius. Though The Hollywood Reporter reports that it caused her to butt heads with Costume Director Ruth Morley on occasion, who “initially envisioned a character who wasn’t so fully formed from a style perspective.” In an interview with People Magazine last summer, Keaton credited her mother with allowing her the space to express herself through her wardrobe, saying, “She was my biggest supporter and manifester of my creativity.” In a true “life imitating art imitating life” scenario on the Vogue World stage, Keaton had added, “Later in life, my inspiration came from countless hours of cutting and pasting my way through magazines like ‘Vogue Magazine.’” Filed under diane keaton hollywood models ralph lauren vogue 10/27/25 Read Next Pamela Anderson turns heads with wild floral outfit at gar...
